rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both heroes share a strong structure, with a large headline, one green primary button, a 14-day trial note and an invoice dashboard mockup. B wins because its visual is cleaner. In A, the tilted email card covers part of one invoice row and the name on the next, which looks messy, and A's bold black 'Watch a demo' link with a play icon competes with the button more than B's quiet underlined grey link. A's serif-italic headline has more personality, but B's left edges line up more neatly and its email and 'opened your reminder' toast tell the product story without clutter. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both heroes are polished and similar in structure. A keeps a cleaner hierarchy: its demo link is a light underlined text link that is clearly quieter than the button, and its invoice card with the email preview is specific to the product and stays calm. In B, the bold 'Watch a demo' with its play icon and the pill-shaped 'Sign in' button pull more attention, and the tilted email card hides invoice rows, which makes the visual busier and more likely to compete with the headline.
